thread:
pagerbot: Pager: SEV2 - runtime OOM/paging surge detected on cluster inference-prod-us-west-2. Service: runtime-inference. Customer impacted: CanvasAI (elevated 5xx + latency). Triggered 2026-03-17T10:02:14Z. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging>.

Dave_oncall: I'm on it, triaging now. Assigning to @alice for telemetry + logs.

Alice: quick snapshot from 10:00-10:05 UTC: GPUs showing high reserved memory and a lot of pagewalks. Pasting condensed nvml and runtime counters:
```
GPU0: total 48GB free 1.2GB resident 46.8GB pagewalks 4.1k
GPU1: total 48GB free 0.9GB resident 47.1GB pagewalks 3.9k
kvcache: entries 1.2M -> growth spike at 10:01 UTC (+420k in 30s)
avg seq len: 256 -> tail at 1024 for some requests
batch_size mean: 12 -> 24 at spike window
```

Alice: logs excerpt (short): s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1765432109/runtime/trace.log.gz

Priya: hypothesis 1 - KV cache grew rapidly due to large batch+long-seq requests; that pushed GPU memory fragmentation -> pagewalks -> OOM/evictions. Hypothesis 2 - a model variant with larger KV footprint got routed during a canary.

Marco: I see corresponding host OOM and kernel page-fault storms in host dmesg on node infer-uw2-gpu-07. NVML shows increased memory allocation retries.

Dave_oncall: Immediate mitigations applied: 1) rollback routing to stable model variant, 2) reduced max_batch_size to 8 via runtime config, 3) triggered kvcache-evict(prefix=recent-heavy) API. Commands: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/runtime/config -d '{"max_batch_size":8}'
POST https://internal-api/eval/kvcache/evict?prefix=recent-heavy
```

Dave_oncall: Applying now — will report back on error rate.

Pagerbot: Auto-update: customer error rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.9% over 2 minutes after changes (10:05 UTC). Latency 95p reduced from 1.9s to 1.1s.

Ian_support: Support called CanvasAI at 10:08 UTC. They reported 502s and request timeouts. They've accepted the temporary rollback and will pause heavy batch workloads for next 2 hours. Logged conversation: https://tickets.redwood/customer/CA-1123

Priya: Quick note: we should collect full timeline + dumps: nvml traces, cgroup stats, runtime heap dump, and route decision logs for 09:58-10:06 UTC. Also capture sample requests that caused long seq lengths.

Alice: collected artifacts: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1765432109/{nvml.gz,host_dmesg.txt,rt_heap.dump,route_logs.jsonl} (upload complete).

Marco: I kicked rolling restart of the 3 most impacted pods (infer-uw2-*) to clear fragmented allocations. Restart outputs: pods restarted at 10:10 UTC, readiness back by 10:12 UTC.

Sre_lead: Good short-term mitigation. For RCA we need: 1) exact model variant IDs routed during spike, 2) batch-size distribution by route, 3) KV cache growth per prefix, 4) whether autoscaler or canary respawned new pods with different runtime config. Assigning to @marco for timeline + draft RCA.

Marco: Taking RCA. Plan: combine route_logs.jsonl + nvml traces + heap dump -> timeline doc. Tentative root-cause: combination of a small canary traffic shift to variant X (higher KV resident), transient traffic spike that increased batch sizes, leading to kvcache growth and fragmentation -> pagewalk storms -> OOM/502s.

Dave_oncall: Notes on mitigations & durable fixes: - enforce per-route max_batch_size caps, - add kvcache backpressure when growth > threshold, - add a probe for model variant KV footprint in canary.

Priya: Also add alert for sudden kvcache entry deltas (e.g., >200k in 1m) and correlate with pagewalk metric.

Ian_support: Customer update sent at 10:20 UTC: "Incident mitigated, continuing monitoring. Appreciated quick response." Support ticket updated.

Pagerbot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Will remain Sev2 until RCA published. Created incident doc ID INC-2026-1765432109.

Marco: Handoff: I'm taking primary for RCA write-up and follow-ups. Handoff to @marco at 10:22 UTC. Next steps checklist posted to thread: - compose timeline (who/when/which pods) - reproduce in staging with variant X + batch patterns - run memory fragmentation experiment - propose safe defaults + canary checks.

Sre_lead: Thanks team. If anything regresses, re-open pager. Leaving notes: patch to runtime to expose per-request kv footprint metrics (telemetry ticket added).

Dave_oncall: closing live coordination. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:

Marco: I'll ping when RCA draft is ready (~ EOB today).
